## Schema consistency

**No runtime schema exists for the `PromptSession` record itself, at any layer.**

- `PromptSession` (`src/renderer/state/promptSessions.ts:29-76`) is a TS-only interface — compile-time, erased at runtime. Data read back from disk is `as`-cast, not parsed.
- The IPC boundary (`ipcSchemas.cjs:217-248`, `promptSessionsMergeActiveIndex`) validates the **envelope** only — id charset/length, map size caps, prototype-pollution guard — but each session value is `z.unknown()`. `status`'s 3-value union, `tag`'s enum, `createdAt` format: none of it is checked on the wire.

The CLI/scheduler path (`epicMint.cjs:216-351`, `ensureEpic`) builds a *different* object literal, with its own id scheme (`psess-<ts>-<seq>` vs `<slug>-<uuid8>`). - `ensureEpic` does enforce one real invariant well: the born-`proposed` law is fail-closed (throws if a mint call passes any status but `proposed`, `epicMint.cjs:299-305`) — so *lifecycle* is actually protected. It's field *shape* that isn't.

## Does the current workflow support dynamic assembly? Not really — for `home` specifically, no.

I checked the actual selection pipeline (`select.ts`'s `scoreVariants` + `selectionPredicates.ts`), not just the library structure.

**How selection actually works:** `scoreVariants` walks a lens's presets in order (v1, v2, …) and picks the first preset whose per-slot choice is "eligible." A variant is only *conditionally* eligible if it has an entry in `VARIANT_REQUIREMENTS` (`selectionPredicates.ts`) — a `requires`/`avoidIf` predicate checked against the project's real `ProjectPageSummary`. **If a variant has no entry there, it's unconditionally eligible, which means preset `v1`'s pick always wins the tie-break, on every run, for every project.**

**`VARIANT_REQUIREMENTS` has exactly two entries in the whole codebase, both in `marketing`:**
```
'marketing.proof.quote': { requires: ['quotes.length > 0'] }
'marketing.proof.stats': { requires: ['stats.length > 0'] }
```

Nothing else — not `home.overview`, not `home.pillars`, not anything in `feature` or `architecture` — has a predicate. So:

- **`home` lens (the one you're asking about): `overview` always resolves to `dashboard`, `pillars` always resolves to `grid` — for every project, every regenerate.** The `ledger`/`rows` alternates exist in the library but the deterministic selector can never reach them; they're only reachable if a human hand-edits `picks.json` directly (which `mergePicks` then preserves).

## The one-line answer

**Agent = who. Skill = a procedure the who reaches for. The agent is always in charge — a skill never is.**

A skill is inert text on disk. It cannot decide to run, cannot decide when it's done, cannot decide to stop. Some agent reads it and follows it. So "Architect using /develop" is the right picture; "/develop using dev-lead" never happens.

## The three axes you actually have

Your repo already separates these cleanly — the confusion is that they *sound* like the same question:

| Axis | Artifact | Question it answers | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Actor** | `~/.claude/agents/*.md` | *Who* is at the keyboard | Whole Epic conversation |
| **Mission** | Tag (`feature`/`bug`/`discussion`) | *What kind* of work this is | Whole Epic, set at birth |
| **Procedure** | Skill (`/develop`, `/builder`) | *How* one recurring task is done | One invocation |

`architect.md` says this explicitly: "Stay agnostic about what kind of work this is… Don't fork `/develop`'s PRD structure into this file." That's the axes staying orthogonal.

They're not two agents sharing a skill. They're at **different points in the pipeline, in different processes**:

```
Human ──talks to──> architect          (interactive, Opus, Epic-long)
                       │
                       │ invokes /develop  ← a procedure, not an agent
                       ▼
                    PRD files on disk     ← the handoff artifact
                       │
                    scheduler spawns claude -p   ← new process, no memory of the above
                       ▼
                    dev-lead              (headless, one PRD, then dies)
                       │
                    reads standards.md    ← executor rules, not a skill
```

| 1. What to build | The PRD body | `/develop`, at authoring time | This one PRD |

| 3. How to finish | FINISH PROTOCOL, appended by the scheduler | `scheduler.cjs`, at dispatch | Every run |

## Where I landed

The goal — *"translate and organize, never hide"* — is achievable, but the current pipeline is **structurally lossy before the renderer ever sees the data**. So Simplified Chat can't be a rendering change; it has to be a change to the classifier's contract. The one-line rule I'd adopt:

> **The classifier is a router, never a filter. Every JSONL line reaches the UI. Known kinds get a designed card; unknown kinds get a generic card. A code change upgrades presentation — it never decides whether something is shown.**

That rule is what makes future Anthropic surfaces (TIPs or anything else) appear *automatically* on the day they ship, instead of silently vanishing until someone notices.
